posts.name: AdamH
posts.cooked:
Hi.

I recently discovered Spirit Island and I'm hooked. I got a few friends hooked as well and I'm planning to show it off to some other regulars at the board gaming group around here.

I'm having trouble actually buying a copy of the game and its expansions. None of the local places here have it in stock and when I look online for it, it's hugely expensive. I'm assuming it's out of print but I haven't seen anything really official on it, despite some cursory Googling. For now, I have a friend who owns a copy and I borrow it when I need to get my fix.

But I'd like to buy my own copy and get a hold of the expansion and new spirits. Ideally I'd like to have it by GenCon in early August, and if I have to buy it there that's OK. What I don't want to happen is for me to not have a copy to play at GenCon, and I'd really like to not have to pay $150+ for the base game and $60 for an expansion.

Is there any official word or at least some good speculation on when there will be more copies of all of these things? And what is the best way to buy them? I can get my local game stores to call me when they get a copy (which has already been set up) but I don't know when to expect that.

Thanks!

-Adam

posts.name: dpt
posts.cooked:
I know that the fifth printing (the one coming with the promos) is much larger than the previous ones. I'm also sure that GtG very much wants product in hand to sell at Gen Con (especially the promos), and I expect they're arranging the production schedule to make that happen (and perhaps reserving some copies from distribution as well).

Based on what you say you're looking for, I think you should be fine buying it at Gen Con, but you might have to get to their stall first thing when it opens.

In terms of where to look for information, I might also check BoardGameGeek. There's a pretty active group over there, although official announcements get posted here first.

posts.name: carnilius
posts.cooked: For the promo Spirits, it is very simple to print and play, as the unique power cards and spirit mat is never shuffled or transferred so even a cheap black and white print is sufficient.  The game creator has posted all the necessary images on BGG.  Certainly it's better to have the actual promo spirit copies, but definitely not necessary if you just want to play with them.

posts.name: AdamH
posts.cooked:
I've played several times (15-20 is my guess), I was borrowing a copy from a friend and playing with other people who had found the game. But now I have my own copy.

We haven't lost in quite a while. I'll frequently ramp up the difficulty when I'm not teaching the game to the point where I'm sure we'll lose but we manage to pull through. I had a 2P game where every single land on the board had at least one blight but we still won with one blight left on the card. Yeah the fire guy was responsible for that one.

 

EDIT: I added some pictures of the storage solution I had come up before the expansion. I managed to fit in everything from the expansion into that same box last night with placeholders for the promo spirits, but I don't have any pictures of that yet.

posts.name: AdamH
posts.cooked:
Played a game last night, 2P with both of the new spirits and the new adversary, difficulty level 3 (which turns out to be really hard) and we forgot to put the new tokens on during setup.

We almost lost. We were going to lose but got bailed out by one of two fear cards, but we managed to pull it back and come out with a dominating victory. Keeper of the Forbidden Wilds is very slow and I did some things that turned out to be not smart.

Anyways, here are some pictures of the storage solution with the expansion added and placeholders for the promo spirits. I had print-and-played them before but I gave those proxies to the person who originally let me borrow their set so I need to make new ones.
